views.name: patient_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX,
  Patient.Admission AS Admission,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday
FROM Patient
views.description: One row per patient exposing basic demographic and admission status fields for cohort filtering and grouping (sex, admission type, birthdays and identification).

views.name: patient_admission_status_counts_by_sex
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pd.SEX AS SEX,
  pd.Admission AS Admission,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pd.ID) AS patient_count
FROM
  patient_demographics pd
GROUP BY
  pd.SEX,
  pd.Admission
views.description: Aggregated counts of patients grouped by SEX and Admission status. Useful for quick comparisons of groups (e.g., male in-patient vs outpatient counts) while remaining general for other sexes or admission codes.

views.name: patient_basic_canonicalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  UPPER(p.SEX) AS SEX,
  CASE
    WHEN p.Admission IN ('+', 'yes', 'Yes', 'Y', 'y', 'TRUE', 'True', 'true', '1') THEN 'ADMITTED'
    WHEN p.Admission IN ('-', 'no', 'No', 'N', 'n', 'FALSE', 'False', 'false', '0') THEN 'NOT_ADMITTED'
    WHEN p.Admission IS NULL OR TRIM(p.Admission) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE UPPER(TRIM(p.Admission))
  END AS Admission_normalized,
  p.Birthday AS Birthday
FROM Patient p
views.description: Canonicalized patient-level fields with Admission normalized to standard tokens and SEX uppercased; preserves one row per patient for downstream joins and counts.

views.name: patient_birthyear
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  P.ID AS ID,
  P.Birthday AS Birthday,
  CASE
    WHEN P.Birthday IS NULL OR trim(P.Birthday) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN instr(P.Birthday, '-') > 0 THEN substr(P.Birthday, 1, instr(P.Birthday, '-') - 1)
    WHEN instr(P.Birthday, '/') > 0 THEN substr(P.Birthday, 1, instr(P.Birthday, '/') - 1)
    WHEN length(P.Birthday) >= 4 THEN substr(P.Birthday, 1, 4)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS birth_year
FROM Patient P
views.description: One row per patient with extracted birth year (as text) to support year-based filters and comparisons.

views.name: examination_by_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Examination.ID AS ID,
  Examination."Examination Date" AS "Examination Date",
  Examination."Diagnosis" AS "Diagnosis",
  Examination."Thrombosis" AS "Thrombosis",
  Examination."Symptoms" AS "Symptoms",
  Examination."ANA" AS "ANA",
  Examination."ANA Pattern" AS "ANA Pattern",
  Examination."aCL IgG" AS "aCL IgG",
  Examination."aCL IgM" AS "aCL IgM",
  Examination."aCL IgA" AS "aCL IgA",
  Examination."KCT" AS "KCT",
  Examination."RVVT" AS "RVVT",
  Examination."LAC" AS "LAC"
FROM Examination
LEFT JOIN Patient ON Examination.ID = Patient.ID
views.description: Examination records linked to patient id. One row per examination (preserves Examination.Date and clinical fields); useful for cohorting patients by exam findings or by exam date ranges.
validated_on: How many female patients who came at the hospital in 1997 was immediately followed at the outpatient clinic?

views.name: examination_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  E."ID" AS "ID",
  E."Examination Date" AS "Examination Date",
  -- numeric measurements preserved as-is
  E."aCL IgG" AS "aCL IgG",
  E."aCL IgM" AS "aCL IgM",
  E."aCL IgA" AS "aCL IgA",
  E."ANA" AS "ANA",
  -- canonicalize ANA Pattern to upper-case trimmed value (NULL if empty)
  CASE
    WHEN trim(E."ANA Pattern") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE upper(trim(E."ANA Pattern"))
  END AS "ANA Pattern",
  -- canonicalize Diagnosis and Symptoms to trimmed values (preserve case)
  CASE
    WHEN trim(E."Diagnosis") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(E."Diagnosis")
  END AS "Diagnosis",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(E."KCT") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(E."KCT")
  END AS "KCT",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(E."RVVT") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(E."RVVT")
  END AS "RVVT",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(E."LAC") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(E."LAC")
  END AS "LAC",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(E."Symptoms") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE trim(E."Symptoms")
  END AS "Symptoms",
  -- Thrombosis kept as integer/flag
  E."Thrombosis" AS "Thrombosis"
FROM "Examination" E
views.description: One normalized row per Examination record, exposing raw measurement columns and canonicalized text fields. Keeps original examination-level columns (no aggregation) and casts/standardizes obvious text fields for consistent comparison.
counter_examples: How many female patients were given an APS diagnosis?

views.name: examination_acl_igm_stats_overall
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  AVG("aCL IgM") AS avg_aCL_IgM,
  COUNT(*) AS count_rows,
  MIN("aCL IgM") AS min_aCL_IgM,
  MAX("aCL IgM") AS max_aCL_IgM,
  -- population standard deviation (sqrt of avg((x-avg)^2))
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE
      SQRT(
        (SUM(("aCL IgM") * ("aCL IgM")) - (SUM("aCL IgM") * SUM("aCL IgM")) / COUNT(*))
        / COUNT(*)
      )
  END AS stddev_aCL_IgM
FROM "Examination"
views.description: Overall aggregate statistics for aCL IgM across all Examination rows: count, mean, min, max, and standard deviation. Grouped at a global level (one row) so callers can compute thresholds like 1.2 * average.

views.name: patients_with_examination_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  MAX(CASE WHEN e.Thrombosis = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AS has_thrombosis_2,
  MAX(CASE WHEN e."ANA Pattern" = 'S' AND (e.ANA IS NOT NULL AND e."ANA Pattern" IS NOT NULL) AND
                (e."ANA Pattern" NOT LIKE '%[^S]%' ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AS has_ana_pattern_S_only,
  MAX(e."aCL IgM") AS max_aCL_IgM,
  (SELECT e2."aCL IgM"
     FROM Examination e2
     WHERE e2.ID = p.ID
       AND e2."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL
     ORDER BY e2."Examination Date" DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS most_recent_aCL_IgM,
  (SELECT e3."Examination Date"
     FROM Examination e3
     WHERE e3.ID = p.ID
     ORDER BY e3."Examination Date" DESC
     LIMIT 1) AS most_recent_examination_date
FROM Patient p
LEFT JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID
GROUP BY p.ID
views.description: One row per Patient.ID indicating whether they have any Examination rows matching certain clinical flags (e.g., Thrombosis values, presence of ANA patterns) plus the patient's max and most recent aCL IgM value. Useful for patient-level cohorts based on examination measurements.

views.name: laboratory_results_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "ID",
  "Date",
  CASE
    WHEN trim("ALB") = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST("ALB" AS REAL)
  END AS "ALB",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(CAST("PLT" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST("PLT" AS INTEGER)
  END AS "PLT",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(CAST("GOT" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST("GOT" AS INTEGER)
  END AS "GOT",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(CAST("GPT" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST("GPT" AS INTEGER)
  END AS "GPT",
  CASE
    WHEN trim(CAST("CRP" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST("CRP" AS REAL)
  END AS "CRP",
  -- bundle remaining raw measurement columns into a JSON-like text for portability
  json_object(
    'LDH', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("LDH" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("LDH" AS INTEGER) END,
    'ALP', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("ALP" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("ALP" AS INTEGER) END,
    'TP',  CASE WHEN trim(CAST("TP" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("TP" AS REAL) END,
    'WBC', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("WBC" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("WBC" AS REAL) END,
    'HGB', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("HGB" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("HGB" AS REAL) END,
    'CRE', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("CRE" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("CRE" AS REAL) END,
    'GLU', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("GLU" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("GLU" AS INTEGER) END,
    'T-CHO', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("T-CHO" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("T-CHO" AS INTEGER) END,
    'TG', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("TG" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("TG" AS INTEGER) END,
    'CPK', CASE WHEN trim(CAST("CPK" AS TEXT)) = '' THEN NULL ELSE CAST("CPK" AS INTEGER) END
  ) AS "other_raw_measures"
FROM "Laboratory"
views.description: Normalized laboratory measurement rows with cleaned numeric casts and canonical NULLs; one row per Laboratory measurement (patient,date).

views.name: laboratory_latest_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.ID,
  l.Date,
  l.GOT,
  l.GPT,
  l.CRP,
  l.WBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.PLT
FROM Laboratory l
JOIN (
  SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS max_date
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
) lm ON l.ID = lm.ID AND l.Date = lm.max_date
views.description: Latest laboratory measurement row per patient (one row per Patient.ID + Date is the latest Date for that patient). Useful to join latest labs to patient cohorts.

views.name: patient_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ID AS ID,
  p.SEX AS SEX,
  p.Birthday AS "Birthday",
  p."First Date" AS "First Date",
  p.Admission AS Admission,
  p.Diagnosis AS Diagnosis
FROM Patient p
views.description: One row per patient with canonical patient identifiers and demographic fields normalized/cleaned (casts left to query).

views.name: laboratory_measurements_43
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "ID",
  "Date",
  "UA",
  "GLU",
  "WBC",
  "HGB",
  "PLT"
FROM "Laboratory"
views.description: Laboratory measurement rows at the measurement-date level (one row per Laboratory.ID + Laboratory.Date) exposing lab analytes including UA; filters for non-null measures are applied by queries.

views.name: patient_laboratory_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Laboratory.ID AS ID,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX,
  Laboratory.Date AS Date,
  Laboratory.UA AS UA
FROM
  Laboratory
JOIN
  Patient ON Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID
views.description: Denormalized view joining Patient to Laboratory at each laboratory measurement row, producing one row per Laboratory.ID + Laboratory.Date with patient demographics and lab values; useful to apply patient-specific thresholds to lab results.

views.name: patient_baseline
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  SEX,
  Birthday,
  "First Date",
  Admission,
  Diagnosis
FROM Patient
views.description: One row per patient with canonical patient-level attributes useful for filtering cohorts (sex, birthday, admission, first/description dates, diagnosis). Normalizes column names and exposes raw values; does not apply question-specific filters.

views.name: laboratory_results_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  "ID",
  "Date",
  "GOT",
  "GPT",
  "LDH",
  "ALP",
  "TP",
  "ALB",
  "UA",
  "UN",
  "CRE",
  "T-CHO",
  "TG",
  "GLU",
  "WBC",
  "RBC",
  "HGB",
  "HCT",
  "PLT",
  "CRP",
  "C3",
  "C4"
FROM "Laboratory"
views.description: One row per laboratory measurement record (one row per Laboratory.ID + Laboratory.Date) exposing raw laboratory analytes and the patient ID for joins. Keeps original numeric values (no aggregation).

views.name: patient_core_47
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday,
  Patient.Diagnosis AS Diagnosis,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX
FROM Patient
views.description: One row per patient capturing stable patient attributes used for joins, filters, and ordering: birthday, diagnosis, sex and primary id. Rows are at patient granularity.

views.name: lab_with_patient_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Laboratory.ID AS ID,
  Laboratory.Date AS Date,
  Laboratory.GPT AS GPT,
  Patient.Birthday AS "Patient.Birthday",
  Patient.Diagnosis AS "Patient.Diagnosis"
FROM Laboratory
JOIN Patient ON Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID
views.description: Denormalized rows that join each Laboratory measurement to its Patient row. One row per Laboratory measurement (Laboratory.ID + Laboratory.Date) with patient attributes included to enable filtering and ordering without extra joins.

views.name: laboratory_most_recent_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT l.ID,
       l.Date,
       l.UN,
       l.GOT,
       l.GPT,
       l.LDH,
       l.CRP
FROM Laboratory l
JOIN (
  SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS Date
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
) latest ON l.ID = latest.ID AND l.Date = latest.Date
views.description: Most recent laboratory measurement per patient (latest Date). Useful for queries that need the latest lab values or to deduplicate multiple lab rows per patient.

views.name: male_patients_with_high_tcho_tests
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Laboratory.ID AS ID,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday,
  Laboratory.Date AS Date,
  Laboratory."T-CHO" AS "T-CHO",
  Patient.SEX AS SEX
FROM Laboratory
JOIN Patient ON Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID
WHERE Patient.SEX = 'M' AND Laboratory."T-CHO" IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized rows for male patients' laboratory test instances where T-CHO is present; exposes patient ID, birthday, test date and T-CHO to enable age-based aggregation per patient or overall cohorts.

views.name: patient_basic_demographics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday,
  CAST((strftime('%Y', 'now') - strftime('%Y', Patient.Birthday))
       - (strftime('%m-%d', 'now') < strftime('%m-%d', Patient.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age_years
FROM Patient
views.description: One row per patient with canonical demographic fields and derived age (years, integer) computed from Birthday relative to current date.

views.name: laboratory_records_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  TG,
  GLU,
  -- CRP in source is TEXT in Laboratory; cast to REAL where possible, keep NULL if empty-string
  CASE
    WHEN trim(CRP) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(CRP AS REAL)
  END AS CRP,
  WBC,
  HGB,
  PLT
FROM Laboratory
views.description: Raw laboratory measurement rows (one row per laboratory test instance) with relevant lab measures preserved and NULL-cleaned where appropriate.

views.name: latest_laboratory_per_patient
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.ID,
  l.Date,
  l.TG,
  l.GLU,
  l.CRP,
  l.WBC,
  l.HGB,
  l.PLT
FROM Laboratory l
JOIN (
  SELECT ID, MAX(Date) AS max_date
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
) latest ON l.ID = latest.ID AND l.Date = latest.max_date
views.description: Latest laboratory record per patient (row = most recent Laboratory.Date for each Laboratory.ID/Patient.ID), exposes latest TG and other lab measures for joins to patient-level analyses.

views.name: laboratory_measurements_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ID,
  Date,
  CPK
FROM
  Laboratory
views.description: Raw laboratory measurement rows keyed by patient and date. Keeps test values as-is (no aggregations) so downstream queries can apply thresholds, time filters, and joins to patients.

views.name: patient_lab_join_55
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Patient.ID AS ID,
  Patient.SEX AS SEX,
  Patient.Birthday AS Birthday,
  Laboratory.Date AS Date,
  Laboratory.CPK AS CPK
FROM Patient
JOIN Laboratory ON Laboratory.ID = Patient.ID
views.description: Denormalized join of patients to their laboratory measurement rows. Exposes patient demographics plus each lab measurement row for cohort selection and counting distinct patients who meet lab criteria.
